Figure 1: KV-Compression Aware Training (KV-CAT). A context a goes through both masked (left) and dense (right) forward passes. In the masked forward pass, routers (orange) compute masks for groups of consecutive layers, marking KV slots as active (green) or inactive (muted green). In the dense forward pass (blue), all KV slots are kept. The output of the masked forward pass is used to compute Lmask, router distributions are used to compute Lbudget, and the outputs of the dense forward pass are used to compute Lanchor. These are jointly used to update the parameters.

Figure 2: KV-CAT speeds up gradient-based KV cache compression. We plot the gap in suffix perplexity under full/compressed-prefix inference throughout gradient-based KV cache optimization. Each panel fixes a different KV keep ratio. Across ratios, the KV-CAT checkpoint achieves a comparable ∆PPL in fewer optimization steps than the base model, yielding up to a 5× speedup.

Table 3: Suffix completion under prefix compression. Each example uses a 768-token prefix and a 256-token suffix. Prefix KVs are compressed using Attention Matching. We report: (1) ∆PPL, the difference in suffix perplexity under the full prefix vs. compressed prefix; (2) KL, the divergence between the two token distributions; and (3) Top-1, percentage of tokens on which the two distributions’ top-1 agree.

Figure 4: KV-CAT speeds up gradient-based KV cache compression. We plot the gap in suffix perplexity under full/compressed-prefix inference throughout gradient-based KV cache optimization. Each panel fixes a different KV keep ratio. Across ratios, the KV-CAT checkpoint achieves a comparable ∆PPL in fewer optimization steps than the base model, yielding up to a 5× speedup.

Figure 3: QWEN2.5-0.5B KV-CAT continued pretraining run. We plot dense validation nexttoken-prediction loss, compressed-path validation next-token-prediction loss, and the realized KV retention ratio over the 5.24B-token KV-CAT continued-pretraining run. The retention trace reports the fraction of KV slots kept by the learned routers, whose budget target is 50%.
